title: Input–output machines and sequence rules
summary: A number goes into a machine and another comes out. Find what the machine does, then find the rule of a number sequence.
guide: This studio follows function machines (Years 3–6) and sequence rules (Year 6). A machine does the same thing to every number that goes in, for example "add 7".
The {{term:input}} is on the left and the {{term:output}} on the right. When we know the output and want the input, we run the machine backwards: instead of adding 7, we subtract 7.
In a two-step machine the order matters: first step one, then step two. To go backwards, start with the last step.

A {{term:sequence}} can be made from the number before (term-to-term, e.g. "double it") or from the position (position-to-term, e.g. "3 × position + 2"). The second kind lets you find the 20th term without writing all the others.
Ask "how do you know?" A rule must work for every row, not just one.

engine.label-step: Each number is the one before times
engine.instruction-jump: What happens from one number to the next?
engine.instruction-type: Find the rule, then type the term.

machine-outputs.title: The add-7 machine
machine-outputs.prompt: This machine adds 7 to every number that goes in. Write the outputs. In the last row 30 came out. What went in?
machine-outputs.hint: For the last row ask yourself: which number becomes 30 when I add 7?
machine-outputs.success: Well done! 9 + 7 = 16 and 15 + 7 = 22. And because 23 + 7 = 30, the last input was 23.
machine-outputs.why: Why did you subtract 7 to find the last input?
machine-outputs.model: The machine added 7 to make 30. So before the machine the number was 7 less: 30 − 7 = 23. To go backwards we do the opposite of what the machine does.

feedback.went-forward: You put 30 through the machine and got 37! But 30 is the output. Go backwards: which number makes 30 when you add 7?
feedback.subtracted: This machine adds 7. It does not take 7 away.
feedback.too-big: One of the numbers is too big. The machine only adds 7.
feedback.too-small: One of the numbers is too small. The machine adds 7.

find-the-rule.title: Find the rule
find-the-rule.prompt: This machine's rule is hidden. Three numbers went in and came out. Guess what it does: choose a sign and type its number.
find-the-rule.hint: "Add 4" turns 2 into 6. Does it turn 5 into 15 too? The rule must work for all three rows.
find-the-rule.success: Yes! The machine multiplies by 3: 2 × 3 = 6, 5 × 3 = 15 and 10 × 3 = 30.
find-the-rule.why: Why is "add 4" not the rule, even though it turns 2 into 6?
find-the-rule.model: Because "add 4" would turn 5 into 9, not 15. A rule is only right when it works for every row. "Multiply by 3" works for all three.

feedback.empty: Choose a sign (+, −, ×, ÷) and type a number.
feedback.one-row-only: Your rule works for just one row. Test it on the other rows too.
feedback.fits-some: That rule works for some rows, but not all. Test it on every row.
feedback.wrong-rule: That rule doesn't fit any row. Look at how 2 became 6 and 5 became 15.

two-step-machine.title: A two-step machine
two-step-machine.prompt: This machine has two steps: first it doubles the number, then it adds 3. Write the outputs. In the last row 13 came out. What went in?
two-step-machine.hint: For 4: first 4 × 2, then + 3. For the last row start at the end: take away 3 first, then halve.
two-step-machine.why: To find the last input, why did you take away 3 first and halve after?
two-step-machine.model: The machine's last step was adding 3. Going backwards we start from the end: undo the adding first (13 − 3 = 10), then undo the doubling (10 ÷ 2 = 5). Like socks and shoes: you take the shoes off first.

feedback.order-swapped: You did the steps the other way round! First × 2, then + 3.
feedback.went-forward: You put 13 through the machine again. But 13 is the output: go backwards through the machine.
feedback.undo-order: To go backwards, start with the last step: take away 3 first, then halve.
feedback.undo-sign: The machine added 3; to go back you must take away 3.
feedback.too-big: One of the numbers is too big. Do the steps one at a time.
feedback.too-small: One of the numbers is too small. Do the steps one at a time.

doubling-sequence.title: Double, double
doubling-sequence.prompt: In this sequence each number is made from the one before. Type what each number is multiplied by, then fill the gaps.
doubling-sequence.hint: 3 then 6; 6 then 12. The gaps are not the same! 6 is how many times 3?
doubling-sequence.success: Right! Each term is double the one before: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96.
doubling-sequence.why: Why do the gaps between the numbers get bigger in this sequence?
doubling-sequence.model: Because we double each time instead of adding the same amount. Each time we add the number itself: 3 to 6 (add 3), 6 to 12 (add 6), 12 to 24 (add 12).

feedback.empty: Fill every gap, and type the multiplier too.
feedback.wrong-step: From 3 to 6 and from 6 to 12, how many times bigger did the number get?
feedback.added-gap: You did 12 + 6. But the gaps are not fixed: each term is double the one before, 12 × 2.
feedback.added-three: You added 3. But from 6 to 12 the jump was 6! The rule is not adding.
feedback.too-big: One of the numbers is too big. Just double.
feedback.too-small: One of the numbers is too small. Each term is double the one before.

position-to-term.title: The 20th term
position-to-term.prompt: Look at the sequence 5, 8, 11, 14, … What are the 10th and 20th terms? Predict first, then find the rule.
position-to-term.hint: The terms go up in 3s, like the 3 times table. Multiply the position by 3. How far off is it?
position-to-term.success: Well done! The rule is 3 × position + 2. Term 10: 10 × 3 + 2 = 32. Term 20: 20 × 3 + 2 = 62.
position-to-term.why: Why is the 20th term not double the 10th term?
position-to-term.model: Each term is "three times the position, plus 2". Doubling 32 counts the 2 twice and gives 64. The right answer is 20 × 3 + 2 = 62. If we call the position n, the rule (nth term) is 3n + 2.

feedback.forgot-add: You only multiplied the position by 3. But term 1 is 5, not 3. How much do you need to add?
feedback.doubled: You doubled the 10th term, so the added 2 was counted twice. Use the rule instead.
feedback.extra-jump: You counted one jump too many. From term 4 to term 10 there are 6 jumps.
feedback.missing-jump: You counted one jump too few. From term 4 to term 10 there are 6 jumps.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Test your rule on term 1: it should give 5.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Test your rule on term 1: it should give 5.
